'''Tenpaku Faith''' (天白信仰) is a form of {{ill|Folk religion|en|Folk religion|qid=Q1068640|lt=folk religion}} found primarily in the eastern half of {{ill|Honshu|en|Honshu|qid=Q13989|lt=Honshū}}. Its distribution centers on {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}} and {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|en|Shizuoka Prefecture|qid=Q131320|lt=Shizuoka Prefecture}}, extending southward to the Nansei and Shima regions of {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}} and northward to {{ill|Iwate Prefecture|en|Iwate Prefecture|qid=Q48326|lt=Iwate Prefecture}}.

Due to the diverse associations with {{ill|Worship of heavenly bodies|ja|星神|2=ja|3=星神|lt=Star deities|2=ja|3=星神|lt=Star deities|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/star deities|13=User:Immanuelle/Worship of heavenly bodies|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[Suijin|water gods]], and prayers for safe childbirth, various studies and interpretations have been conducted. Since the 1980s, the faith has often been linked to the ancestral deity of the {{ill|Asami clan|ja|麻積氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asami clan|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Tenpakuhahajin (天白羽神, also known as {{ill|Nagashirahano no Kami|lt=Nagashirahano no Kami|lt=Nagashirahahajin|ja|長白羽神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagashirahahajin|qq=}}), worshipped at the {{ill|Hatadono Shrines|lt=Hatadono Shrines|lt=Hashiro Shrine|ja|機殿神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hashiro Shrine|qq=}} in the ancient province of Ise.

== History of Research ==
Shun'ichirō Mitoshi noted that the earliest studies on Tenpaku faith date back to the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}. In the linguistic dictionary *Wakun no Shiori* compiled by {{ill|Tanikawa Kotosuga|en|Tanikawa Kotosuga|qid=Q6536708|lt=Tanikawa Kotosuga}}, there is a reference to "numerous shrines in Ise Province called Tenpaku Daimyōjin, though their exact nature is unclear." Similarly, *Chōshū Fushi* mentions the Tenpaku Shrine in Ōya Village (now {{ill|Q20037247|ja|大矢町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōya Town|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q20037247}} in {{ill|Inazawa|en|Inazawa|qid=Q389562|lt=Inazawa City}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|en|Aichi Prefecture|qid=Q80434|lt=Aichi Prefecture}}), suggesting it was dedicated to {{ill|Venus|en|Venus|qid=Q313|lt=Venus}}, referred to as Taibakusei (太白星). In 1862, Takahira Nakamura theorized in *Suruga Shiryō* that the deity might represent a synthesis of Tianyi (天一) and Taibai (太白) deities.

In 1909, the folklorist {{ill|Kunio Yanagita|en|Kunio Yanagita|qid=Q971687|lt=Yanagita Kunio}} explored Tenpaku in *Life of the Mountain People*. In subsequent works, he dismissed earlier speculative theories, proposing that Tenpaku was likely connected to {{ill|Fūjin|en|Fūjin|qid=Q1483957|lt=Wind deities}}. This theory gained significant attention among later scholars.

From the post-World War II period, research on Tenpaku progressed. {{ill|Yoshio Hotta|ja|堀田吉雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshio Horita|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q56348851}}, a disciple of Yanagita, published several studies between 1951 and 1964. While he leaned toward the theory of Tenpaku being a fusion of Chinese deities Tianyi and Taibai, he remained cautious, awaiting further evidence.

In 1971, Nokiku Imai compiled a detailed map of Tenpaku shrines in *Great Tenpaku Kami*, asserting that the faith predates wet-rice cultivation and reaches back to the {{ill|Jōmon period|en|Jōmon period|qid=Q52824|lt=Jōmon period}}. The publication also included analyses suggesting connections to {{ill|Natural disaster|ja|風水害|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/flood control|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 自然災害|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8065}}, Tibetan Lamaist sexual symbolism, and the deity Tenpakuhahajin.

Building on Imai's research, Sōmoku Yamada conducted in-depth surveys in five prefectures (Mie, Aichi, Nagano, Shizuoka, and Yamanashi), which he serialized as *Tenpaku Chronicles* in 1977. He proposed that Tenpaku's origins lie in the deity Tenpakuhahajin.

== Places Associated with Tenpaku ==
{{Seealso|{{ill|Tenpaku|ja|天白|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenpaku|qq=}}}}
=== Aichi Prefecture ===
* {{ill|Tenpaku River|ja|天白川 (愛知県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenpaku River (Aichi)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11443111}} - A river flowing through {{ill|Nisshin, Aichi|en|Nisshin, Aichi|qid=Q696777|lt=Nisshin}} and {{ill|Nagoya|en|Nagoya|qid=Q11751|lt=Nagoya}}, named after a shrine to Tenpaku deity in its lower reaches.
* {{ill|Tenpaku-ku|en|Tenpaku-ku|qid=Q1155245|lt=Tenpaku Ward}} - A ward of Nagoya named after the river.
* {{ill|Tenpaku|ja|天白村 (愛知県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenpaku Village (Aichi)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17177017}} - Formerly in Nagoya, named after the river.
* Tenpaku River - A small river in {{ill|Higashiura|en|Higashiura|qid=Q677745|lt=Higashiura Town}}, also associated with the Tenpaku deity.<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=張州府志 第6|year=1916|publisher=名古屋史談会}}</ref>
* {{ill|Tenpaku-chō, Okazaki|ja|天白町 (岡崎市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenpaku Town (Okazaki)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17218861}} - A town in {{ill|Okazaki, Aichi|en|Okazaki, Aichi|qid=Q242783|lt=Okazaki}}, named after the Tenpaku deity.
* {{ill|Tenpaku River|ja|天白川 (田原市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenpaku River (Tahara)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q132044415}} - A river flowing through {{ill|Tahara, Aichi|en|Tahara, Aichi|qid=Q501891|lt=Tahara City}}.

=== Mie Prefecture ===
* {{ill|Tenpaku River|ja|天白川 (三重県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenpaku River (Mie)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17174431}} - A river in {{ill|Yokkaichi|en|Yokkaichi|qid=Q26410|lt=Yokkaichi}}.
* {{ill|Tenpaku|ja|天白村 (三重県)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenpaku Village (Mie)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17175728}} - Formerly part of {{ill|Matsusaka|en|Matsusaka|qid=Q460829|lt=Matsusaka}}.
